{
  "subtype": "exploratory_data_analysis",
  "focus_variable": "label_pos",
  "per_column": [
    {
      "name": "review_aspect_domain",
      "role": "predictor",
      "is_predictor": true,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": true,
      "rationale": "Product category domain is an external, interpretable segmentation independent of sentiment; one can compare positive/negative rates across media vs physical vs food."
    },
    {
      "name": "product_quality_signal",
      "role": "restatement",
      "is_predictor": false,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": true,
      "rationale": "Praised/criticized/mixed quality is essentially the sentiment expressed about the product, strongly collinear with label_pos; it largely restates the focus rather than opening an external relationship."
    },
    {
      "name": "emotional_intensity",
      "role": "predictor",
      "is_predictor": true,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": true,
      "rationale": "Intensity is a separate dimension from valence; positive and negative reviews can both be intense, so it supports meaningful cross-tabulation with sentiment. Categories are well-separated ordinal levels."
    },
    {
      "name": "negative_emotion_type",
      "role": "restatement",
      "is_predictor": false,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": true,
      "rationale": "Presence/type of negative emotion is nearly definitional of negative sentiment; heavily collinear with label_pos, so it mostly restates the focus."
    },
    {
      "name": "positive_emotion_type",
      "role": "restatement",
      "is_predictor": false,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": true,
      "rationale": "Presence/type of positive emotion is nearly definitional of positive sentiment; strongly collinear with label_pos and largely restates the focus."
    },
    {
      "name": "expectation_outcome",
      "role": "predictor",
      "is_predictor": true,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": true,
      "rationale": "Whether expectations were met is correlated with but conceptually distinct from valence; well-separated ordinal categories allow interpretable segmentation of how outcomes relate to sentiment."
    },
    {
      "name": "defect_type",
      "role": "predictor",
      "is_predictor": true,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": true,
      "rationale": "Type of defect is an external, interpretable categorical facet; while defects skew negative, the specific defect category (hardware, content, durability) offers meaningful segmentation beyond bare sentiment."
    },
    {
      "name": "recommendation_stance",
      "role": "restatement",
      "is_predictor": false,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": true,
      "rationale": "Recommend vs discourage is essentially a proxy for sentiment polarity, highly collinear with label_pos, so it mostly restates the focus rather than opening a new relationship."
    }
  ],
  "n_predictors": 4,
  "relationship_informativeness": 0.55,
  "rationale": "The set is well-formed with interpretable, well-separated categorical scales suitable for grouping and cross-tabulation against sentiment. However, roughly half the columns (product_quality_signal, negative_emotion_type, positive_emotion_type, recommendation_stance) are near-tautological with the sentiment label and largely restate the focus, limiting genuine discovery. The remaining columns (aspect_domain, emotional_intensity, expectation_outcome, defect_type) do open external, informative relationships—covering product domain, arousal, expectation dynamics, and failure modes—making the set moderately, but not strongly, informative for exploratory analysis."
}
